3 ArcadeDB containers on one Docker network, bind-mounted so data survives a restart.
SERVER_LIST = arcadedb-0:2434:2480,... quorum=majority (persistent: databases + replication bind-mounted)
All containers start in parallel; Testcontainers waits for each node's HTTP health probe.
Every node's cluster endpoint is polled once a second until one of them claims leadership.
GET /api/v1/cluster -> body contains "isLeader":true (the run fails after 60s)
Database and schema are written through the leader, which Raft carries to every follower.
CREATE VERTEX TYPE User, Photo - EDGE TYPE HasUploaded, FriendOf, Likes - UNIQUE_HASH / FULL_TEXT / GEOSPATIAL
Schema and data are verified on all three nodes before anything is broken.
db0/db1/db2.checkSchema(); until(countUsers() == 10 on all three) atMost 30s
A Docker network disconnect is a true symmetric partition - the leader lands alone in the minority.
A leader that cannot reach a majority steps down by itself; only the two-node side can elect.
The majority partition keeps serving writes while the isolated node is stuck with its pre-partition data.
Reconnecting is not enough: the gRPC channels back off for ~2 minutes, so the node is restarted.
reconnectToNetwork(...); container.stop(); container.start(); waitForContainerHealthy(90); new ServerWrapper(...)
All three nodes must reach the count the majority reached while the partition was open.
until(restarted == majorityCount && s1 == majorityCount && s2 == majorityCount) atMost 180s
